html:
The settlement of New England by about 20,000 English Puritans in the two decades from 1620, most of them in the 1630s.

Puritans wanted to purify the Church of England of Catholic practices. Under King Charles I and Archbishop Laud they felt pressed and feared for their faith. The Pilgrims of the Mayflower, who signed the Mayflower Compact, came first in 1620. In 1630 John Winthrop led a large fleet to found the Massachusetts Bay Colony and Boston, hoping to build a model Christian community.

Unlike most early colonists, they came as whole families, often with some money and skills. Their towns grew fast and stable. They founded Harvard College in 1636, and groups that disagreed split off to found Connecticut and Rhode Island.

The flow stopped around 1640 when the English Civil War began, and many Puritans stayed home to fight. Their descendants gave New England its churches, town meetings and schools, and its later habit of trading by sea.
sum: The settlement of New England by about 20,000 English Puritans in the two decades from 1620, most of them in the 1630s.
